newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Rains delay Hungarian cereals harvest. [CORRECTED 15:38 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Rains delay Hungarian cereals harvest. [CORRECTED 15:38 GMT]

text.p: Rains in Hungary have delayed harvesting by at least one week, officials said on Monday.
"It is safe to say that harvesting has been delayed by at least one week," Zsolt Kiraly of the Agriculture Ministry told Reuters.
He added that wheat, oats and rye harvesting was likely to be finished around August 20 at the earliest.
Attila Bussay of the National Meteorological Service (OMSZ) said that over the past five days only north Hungarian counties saw significant rains of 55-60 millimetres.
He added that even moderate rains could delay harvesting and were also likely to reduce the quality of the wheat crop.
But he said current weather conditions were favourable for maize.
"Weather that is bad for wheat harvesting is usually good for maize," he said, adding, however, that temperatures were below what was ideal for maize.
"Maize likes hot and humid weather. In Hungary, you either have hot and dry or cold and humid weather".
Market participants expected this year's maize crop to slightly exceed last year's already good six million tonnes.

Latest trade estimates put this year's wheat crop at between four and 4.5 million tonnes, compared with 3.9 million in 1996 and earlier ministry estimates of five million tonnes, but with a relatively high percentage of low-quality wheat.
Traders said earlier that this year the customary 60-40 milling to feed wheat ratio was more likely to be 40-60.
However, ministry officials said it was too early to give even a rough estimate of wheat quality.
"Less than one third of the wheat has been harvested and most producers start harvesting on their best lots," Kiraly said.
The agriculture ministry's Balazs Tarjan (corrects spelling) added that producers and traders had different interests, but noted that wheat futures prices were rising.
Current weather forecasts point to scattered showers over the northern half of Hungary and moderate to heavy rains throughout the country by Friday.
